question_data.Question: 이 글에서 글쓴이가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
question_data.Paragraph: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, allowing us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. Companies large and small have off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. With air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
question_data.Options: ① We should recognize that computerization has not freed consumers from routine work. ### ② We should replace travel agents because online reservations require less consumer effort. ### ③ We should judge technological progress chiefly by the efficiency gains of companies. ### ④ We should expect self-service systems to increase the leisure time of consumers. ### ⑤ We should treat extra consumer tasks as evidence of improved company service.
question_data.Explanation: ①가 정답입니다. 필자는 컴퓨터화가 반복 노동을 줄여 여가를 늘릴 것이라는 약속과 달리, 기업의 일이 소비자에게 넘어와 오히려 시간이 줄었다고 지적한다. 따라서 소비자가 반복 업무에서 해방되지 못한 현실을 인식하라는 ①이 취지에 맞는다. ③는 소비자의 부담을 빼고 기업 효율만 보며, ④은 지문의 현실과 반대이다. ②의 수고 감소와 ⑤의 서비스 개선도 예약·포장·계산을 소비자가 맡게 된다는 비판을 왜곡한다.
